---
title: "Problem & Urgency"
subtitle: "Why shortcut learning is the #1 blocker for LLM deployment"
---

## The Core Problem

- LLMs **memorize surface patterns** (keyword co-occurrence, number magnitude, answer position) instead of learning genuine reasoning
- Models score high on benchmarks — then **fail silently** on real-world inputs that differ even slightly from training data
- Enterprise evaluations routinely show **20–40pp accuracy drops** between clean benchmarks and distribution-shifted test sets
- **This is not a minor quality issue — it is a deployment blocker**

---

## Why Now

- **Regulated domains adopting LLMs** — finance, healthcare, legal now require robustness evidence; silent failure is unacceptable
- **Fine-tuning is the standard adaptation path** — and it *amplifies* shortcut reliance (smaller domain corpora are more pattern-rich)
- **No production tooling exists** — current mitigations (data augmentation, manual red-teaming) are expensive, ad hoc, and incomplete
- **EU AI Act & FDA AI/ML guidance** increasingly mandate demonstrable robustness for high-risk AI systems

---

## Real-World Impact

| Domain | Shortcut Failure Mode | Consequence |
|--------|----------------------|-------------|
| **Finance** | Keys on revenue alone, ignores margin + debt | Confident wrong credit decisions |
| **Medical** | Memorizes symptom-diagnosis co-occurrence | Fails on novel presentations |
| **Legal** | Pattern-matches jurisdiction keywords | Misapplies precedent under new facts |
| **Any adversarial setting** | Surface patterns exploited by adversaries | Systematic evasion of model checks |

::: {.callout-important}
**Trust is the bottleneck, not capability.** Buyers need proof that models reason correctly — not just that they score well.
:::
